div.head: Northu 5
div.ab: Gif preost dom to læwedum sceote, þe he to gehadedum scolde, gilde XX ór.
Gif preost dom to læwedum sceote, þe he to gehadedum scolde, gilde XX or.
Wenn ein Priester ein Processurtheil, das er bei Geistlichen [nachsuchen] sollte, an Laien überträgt, zahle er 20 Ör.
If a priest refers to laymen a judgment which he should [seek] from clergy, let him pay 20 ores.
If a priest refers a case to a layman which he ought to refer to an ecclesiastic, he is to pay 20 ores.
If a priest turns judgment in a dispute over to a layman, when he should refer it to an ecclesiastic, he is to pay twenty oras.
div.note: Some of Liebermann’s notes here are cut off in the gutter of the scan used, and are still to be completed.
Liebermann compares the Canons of Edgar.

note.seg: sacu (Prozesssache zwischen Priestern), schreibt Can. Edg., sollen geferan oder Bischof schlichten. Bischöfe sollen ihren Streit na sceotan to læwedum mannum; Polity 10 p. 428. [Ich glaube nicht mit Böhmer Ki. u. Staat 48, dass sich die Geistlichen nicht beim Spruche ihrer Oberen zu beruhigen brauchten.] Vgl. Gl Geistliches Gericht 19

sacu (a lawsuit between priests), writes Can. Edg., is to be settled by the geferan or the bishop. Bishops are not to refer their dispute to laymen, na sceotan to læwedum mannum; Polity 10 p. 428. [I do not believe, with Böhmer Ki. u. Staat 48, that the clergy did not need to accept the decision of their superiors.] Cf. Gl Geistliches Gericht 19
Also ‘Ungehorsam’ des Bischofs; s. o. 2, 2¹. Da von einer Ungehorsamsbusse gegen die geferan (s. vor. Anm.) keine Rede, richtet hier der Bischof allein
Thus ‘disobedience’ towards the bishop; see above 2, 2¹. Since there is no mention of a fine for disobedience towards the geferan (see preceding note), the bishop judges alone here
